subject: calderMobile
pitch:
Category: Abstract.
Subject: hanging mobile.
Style: Alexander Calder.
reasoning:
I'm thinking about building a Calder-style hanging mobile rather than a creature standing on the ground—since it hangs from a point above, its lowest elements won't necessarily touch the floor the way a standing model would.

I'm planning a recursive wire-and-shape structure: a top hook, descending arms with balanced spans, and flat painted shapes (black, red, yellow, blue, white) suspended from thin wire drops, building out helper functions for arms, wires, and hung shapes rather than using joints since everything stays static.

Now I'm defining the shape outlines themselves — ellipses, leaves, crescents — as extruded flat polygons with adjustable yaw rotation, generating point arrays for each outline type to give the mobile its variety of Calder-style forms.

Let me instead compute the inner circle radius so it actually passes through the same tip points as the outer arc, solving for the correct matching radius and angle so the crescent closes smoothly rather than leaving a blunt edge.

I'm picking a Calder-style flat gouache palette with black, red, yellow, blue, and white, and writing a paint function that adds slight mottled noise for a hand-painted feel. I'm also considering adding a subtle decorative texture, like a small spiral motif, on one of the discs for visual interest.

Now I'm sketching out the vertical layout of the mobile, starting from a ceiling hook near the top and working down through a suspension ring to the first main arm, planning rough heights and horizontal spans for the balance of the piece.

Still writing arm geometry logic...

Now I'm sketching the mobile tree structure itself: pivot P0 with asymmetric arm lengths and a slight tilt, branching into sub-arm B (holding a red disc and black leaf) and sub-arm C, each hanging from wires off the main arm's ends rather than their centers.

For grounding, instead of computing coordinates precisely upfront, I'll build the whole tree then measure its bounding box and shift the root group's y-position so the lowest point sits at zero -- since the root is static with no joints, translating it afterward is safe.

Now I'm designing the data structure for the mobile: shapes and arms form a recursive tree, where each arm has a left/right hang point and tilt, and each hang references another node with a drop length. The build function takes a node and its attachment top point -- for shapes that's the top edge, for arms it's the pivot -- then recursively draws wires down to each child's attach point.

I'm adding yaw rotation per arm so the mobile reads as a 3D structure rather than flat, computing each arm's end positions using a direction vector based on that yaw angle, plus a tiny bead/eyelet at hang points for visual detail.

For the arm shapes themselves, I'm sweeping a curved path through the two end points and the pivot using a Catmull-Rom spline with slight vertical/side bowing for a hand-forged Calder look, with small torus hooks at the ends and a thin wire radius.

Adding wire hooks at the pivot...

Now I'm defining shape outlines for the charms — disc, oval, leaf, crescent, kidney — each built from a small set of points scaled by size, with some curves marked sharp or smoothed for a more organic silhouette.

For the extrude call I'll position shapes at the computed center with proper orientation, thickness and bevel settings. I'll avoid importing types from the builder package directly since that's risky, defining my own point type instead, and I'll only apply smoothing to the leaf and triangle shapes to avoid issues with sharp corners.

For the twisting motion characteristic of Calder shapes, I'll skip full tilt and just add yaw rotation for simplicity. For the material, I'm thinking through a gouache-style paint approach using mottle to blend the base color with a darker shade for a hand-painted texture effect.

Now I'm working out wire color (flat black) and adding decorative details to the white disc shapes—concentric rings and a dot pattern rendered via a plane geometry positioned just off the disc's surface, using its normal vector to offset correctly. I'm keeping yaw at zero for these decal elements so the normals stay simple along the Z-axis.

Working through the normal vector math for angled decal placement...

I'm also considering adding a Calder-style touch with a yellow disc featuring black polka dots, plus maybe a small ceiling hook made from a torus ring to hang the whole mobile.

Now I'm designing the tree data structure for the mobile, defining arms that can hold multiple hanging elements at different distances along their length, with helper functions to construct shapes and arms consistently.

I'm working out the geometry: each arm's height at a given distance depends on its tilt, its direction depends on yaw, and wires drop from arm points to the tops of child shapes. I'm also thinking about balance roughly, placing heavier shapes closer to the pivot, and starting to sketch the actual tree with a root arm.

Continuing to build out the mobile tree, nesting arm B, arm C, and arm D underneath the root, each with its own yaw and tilt, hanging a mix of discs, leaves, and crescents at varying distances and sizes.

I'll wire a top ring down to the pivot, starting the arm's y-position at 2.0 before adjusting later. For the bounding box, I'm computing it from the root object and shifting the root's position so it sinks to the ground properly, then defining the node types for shapes and arms in the mobile structure.

For the arm nodes, I'm computing the hanging positions by sampling points along the arm's length, adding a slight sag and lateral wobble using sine functions, then building a smooth curved path through these points and sweeping a thin wire geometry along it to create the physical arm connecting the pivot to its hanging shapes.

Adding paint colors and the hook torus geometry with its connecting rod, then starting on outline generator functions for different shade shapes like disc and oval using polar coordinate arrays.

Still writing texture code...
